en: Ambrosio Rianzares Bautista wrote and read the 1898 Philippine Declaration of Independence, not Andres Bonifacio.
Ferdinand Magellan arrived in 1521, but Miguel Lopez de Legazpi established the first permanent Spanish settlement in 1565.
Marcela Agoncillo and her daughters sewed the first official Philippine flag, not Emilio Aguinaldo.
The Philippine legislative branch is not unicameral; it is a bicameral Congress composed of the Senate and House of Representatives.
The national bird, the Philippine eagle, eats more than just monkeys, including flying foxes and snakes.
Filipino and English are both official languages of the Philippines, not just Filipino.
The Sinulog festival actually honors the Santo Niño, the Holy Child Jesus, not Ferdinand Magellan.
The President, not the Chief Justice, serves as the head of the executive branch of government.
Julian Felipe only composed the music for the national anthem, while Jose Palma wrote the original Spanish lyrics.
The Philippines did not gain independence from Spain on July 4; that 1946 date marks independence from the United States.
The Igorots are not a single unified tribe, but several distinct ethnolinguistic groups with unique cultures and languages.
The Sampaguita, our national flower, is actually native to other parts of Asia, not exclusively the Philippines.
